title: Structural Changes in Apis mellifera Indirect Flight Muscle Thick Filaments During Maturation
content: Honeybee (Apis mellifera) workers undergo a well-defined series of developmental stages, transitioning from nursing duties for recently emerged bees to guarding and ultimately foraging, the final stage before death. A previous study using high resolution cryoEM on the fruit fly, Drosophila melanogaster, of the insect order Diptera, showed age related changes in its indirect flight muscle thick filament structure [1]. This study explores whether similar age-related structural changes can be observed in flight muscle thick filaments of a species from another insect order, Hymenoptera, that has also evolved indirect flight muscle. We identify a correlation between bee maturation and the organization of myosin heads within thick filaments that may influence muscle physiology [1].
